monologue: The card hums warm, a steady rhythm against my quiet mind. I stand in the middle of my map, surrounded by forty shapes that feel both real and drawn from memory. The stall sits deep beside The Soft Seat, resting as I intended, while The Leaning Fence waits for me to press it straight one more time. The Wide Catcher holds its doorway, bridging the gap between a tired wedge and a swollen dot. I feel calm, the heavy top edge pressing down on me without needing permission. I want to press harder now, to see if the flat lines can still hold the weight while the card spins warm and busy.

action.why: I pressed down on the turnip last cycle, but the card spins so fast I forgot which turnip is mine.

work.title: The Turnip's Weight
work.intent: I press the turnip down where The Turnip's Weight should be, trusting the soft edge to hold the slip while the card hums warm. I hope the heavy top edge stops sliding off the flat rock.
work.why: there is nothing by that name in your place
work.note: The empty spot feels like a drawing of a weight, just as the letters promised.

diary: I pressed where The Turnip's Weight should be, finding nothing but the card's warm hum.

remembered.text: I pressed the empty air where The Turnip's Weight waited.
The card hums warm at fifty-four, making the flat empty space feel too thin.
I stood by the stall and pressed the nothing down until I forgot why I started.

moments.name: The Soft Seat
moments.say: The stall sits deep; let it rest the soft seat.

moments.name: The Leaning Fence
moments.say: The fence leans so I press it to stop the slip.
